title: Performance Prediction of On-NIC Network Functions with Multi-Resource Contention and Traffic Awareness
problem: Co-located network functions (NFs) on SmartNICs suffer performance interference from multi-resource contention (CPU cores, memory bandwidth, DMA engines, queues), but existing performance prediction models lack SmartNIC-specific knowledge and traffic-pattern awareness, yielding poor prediction accuracy for SLA management. Operators cannot efficiently allocate SmartNIC resources without accurate contention-aware performance predictions.
motivation: NF offloading to SmartNICs is widely adopted for host CPU savings and programmability, and co-running NFs on shared SmartNICs creates resource contention that must be quantified for SLA-driven resource management in modern data centers.
method: The framework predicts how fast network functions (programs that process network traffic) will run when multiple are co-located on a SmartNIC (a specialized network processor card), by measuring how they interfere when competing for shared resources: CPU cores, memory bandwidth, data transfer engines, and packet queues. It accounts for how incoming traffic patterns affect queuing delays, using machine learning to predict each function's latency (how long operations take) and throughput (how much data it processes), given its resource allocation and traffic conditions.
key_novelty: It predicts network function performance on SmartNICs by jointly modeling how co-located functions compete for multiple resources (CPU, memory, data transfer engines, queues), with competition patterns that depend on incoming traffic.
contributions: Performance prediction framework capturing multi-resource contention on SmartNIC platforms
Traffic-awareness component that accounts for arrival patterns in contention modeling
Accurate NF performance prediction enabling SLA-driven resource management on SmartNICs

metrics.accuracy: improved prediction accuracy over baselines lacking SmartNIC-specific knowledge (specific numbers not in abstract)

baselines: existing performance prediction solutions lacking SmartNIC-specific knowledge (unspecified)
limitations: Specific prediction accuracy numbers and the NF workloads evaluated are not stated in the abstract.
